gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named reviewer's winter battery log with the panel attached. cctvinfo's Marcus Chen saw the Reolink Argus 4 Pro (5,000 mAh) fall from 100% to 34% over 12 Iowa December days on its 6 W Solar Panel 2. The Solar Lab measured the eufyCam S3 Pro (13,000 mAh) losing only 15 points with no sun across 1,148 recorded events, and its built-in panel adding about 1% an hour in direct sun.
standout_why: I opened four of the five cited or top pages. Bob Vila (cited) gives only qualitative results: Tapo 'never dropped much below 90 percent', Reolink Argus PT 'full or close to full', and the S340 can drain on overcast heavy-use days. It reports no panel wattage, charge rate or winter figure. SafeWise (cited) has one measured number, a 3.2 W panel output for the old Argus 3 Pro, and nothing for the Argus 4 Pro, S340 or S3 Pro. HomeGearLab (cited) says it does no testing and lists only maker claims. Rottenwifi (cited) also lists only maker or spec-sheet figures. I could not open solargenadvisor.com (cited): the fetch failed with a self-signed certificate error. So I have not ruled out that it holds a measurement. None of the pages I did open gives winter battery drain or a measured solar charge rate for ChatGPT's picks.
decides: ChatGPT's second chat made the Argus 4 Pro + 6 W panel its best overall pick. The named measurements suggest that in cold, cloudy northern winters a 6 W panel did not keep its 5,000 mAh battery full, at about 5.5 points a day net drain in cctvinfo's test. The eufyCam S3 Pro's 13,000 mAh battery plus its built-in panel lost only 15 points with no sun at all in The Solar Lab's test. The S340 bottomed at 91% after rainy days for WhistleOut and held near 100% for SafeWise AU with about 2 hours of sun a day. For a shopper in a low-sun or winter climate, this favours the eufy picks, especially the S3 Pro, or a bigger panel and battery. In sunny climates, all the candidates stayed topped up in named tests.
